Chilling: 4–10 hours|difficulty=2 | Yield = 1 quart | Servings = Approximately 4 | Rating = 2 }} {{recipe}} | [[Cookbook:Vegan cuisine|Vegan cuisine]] | [[Cookbook:Beverages|Beverages]] '''Rice milk''' is one of the cheapest dairy alternatives to make at home. This simple but highly customizable recipe is great for anyone looking to avoid animal products, additives, and hormones. ==Ingredients== *1 [[Cookbook:Cup|cup]] cooked [[Cookbook: Rice|rice]] *4 cups [[Cookbook:water|water]] ==Procedure== #Combine ingredients in a [[Cookbook:Blender|blender]]. Add sweetener and variations (below) to taste. #Blend until smooth, roughly 1–2 minutes #Refrigerate at least 4 hours or overnight if possible, and use within 5 days. ==Notes, tips, and variations== * Rice milk is easy to customize. White, brown, or even [[Cookbook:Wild Rice|wild rice]] can be used. For new flavors, try adding [[Cookbook:Cocoa Powder|cocoa powder]], [[Cookbook:Vanilla|vanilla]], or [[Cookbook:Banana|banana]]. * For a vegan [[Cookbook:Horchata|horchata]], add 1 tablespoon vanilla and 2 tablespoons [[Cookbook:Cinnamon|cinnamon]] to the rice milk. * This recipe's quantities can be adjusted, keeping a 1:4 ratio of rice to water. *If the milk seems too grainy, the rice can be soaked in water overnight before cooking, or strained through [[Cookbook:Cheesecloth|cheesecloth]] after blending. == See also == * [[Cookbook:Horchata|Horchata]] [[Category:Recipes using rice]] [[Category:Recipes for plant milk]] [[Category:Refrigerated recipes]]
